The bundle share and top-3 share are both 1.0, so supply is concentrated. Sell pressure is almost nil in the early window (sell-to-buy ratio 0.0003), which is what you'd expect when one party holds the coin rather than a crowd of holders.

The recent 15-minute window shows 281 buyers and 41.96 SOL bought against 24.06 SOL sold, but that is a small share of the early operator volume, and the 1% return doesn't show demand that will persist. The 30-minute high is also the current price, so there's no dip to buy into. Operator-backed coins in this class have been roughly break-even, and after a 1.4-5.1% round trip cost, the expected value of a $20 entry is negative.

Verdict: skip. The honest case for demand is weak, and the structure points to a coin whose price depends on the operator's next move rather than on organic buyers.

That is a coordinated operator accumulation, and the operator holds nearly all the supply. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0003 in the launch window means almost nothing was sold early, so the float is thin and controlled.

The last 15 minutes show net flow of +17.89 SOL, but only 28 sellers against 281 buyers, and a 1% return. Because the operator sits on most of the position, a single large exit against a pool of about 3,600 SOL could move price sharply, and a $20 ticket would be exposed to that move plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs. A 2.8% 30-minute return is smaller than that friction. Skip.
